title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.38. (S,τ) is a topological space and T ⊂ S is τ-closed (T = |C|, S = |F| for a sub-figure C ⊂ F). τ'_0 is a topology on T finer than the induced topology τ_0. Grothendieck looks for the topologies τ' on S that (1) are finer than τ and (2) induce τ'_0 on T, and wants the coarsest one.

Candidate. Declare closed all sets A ∪ B, with A ⊂ S τ-closed and B ⊂ T τ'_0-closed.
- Induced topology on T: (A∪B)∩T = (A∩T)∪B. Here A∩T is τ_0-closed, hence τ'_0-closed, so the trace is τ'_0-closed.
- Finite unions: obviously stable.
- Arbitrary intersections: he uses the distributive identity ∩_{i∈I}(A_i∪B_i) = ∪_{J⊂I}(∩_{i∈J}A_i ∩ ∩_{j∉J}B_j).
- Induced topology on U = S∖T: (A∪B)∩U = A∩U, so it is τ|U, i.e. unchanged.
- Minimality: in any such τ', T is closed (since τ' is finer than τ). So each τ'_0-closed B ⊂ T is τ'-closed, and τ' must contain all A∪B.

Unfinished converse. He starts a crossed-out argument: if τ' ≤ τ, τ'|T = τ'_0 and τ'|U = τ|U, then τ' is the topology above. This is abandoned.

Oblique margin. He starts characterising closed sets X intrinsically via the pair (B, U) = (X∩T, X∩U), with the condition B ⊃ (closure of X_U) ∩ T. This becomes the lemma on p.40: X is τ'-closed iff
1. X_U is closed in U;
2. X_T is τ'_0-closed;
3. cl_τ(X_U) ∩ T ⊂ X_T.

Modern reading. τ' is the join τ ∨ σ in the lattice of topologies, where σ has as closed sets S and the τ'_0-closed subsets of T. Equivalently, it is the recollement (open U / closed T gluing) of (U, τ|U) and (T, τ'_0), with the same gluing datum as before. The point is the 'algebra of figures': refining the structure on a closed sub-figure extends canonically and minimally to the ambient figure.
errors: The intersection argument has a gap for infinite I. The distributive formula expresses ∩(A_i∪B_i) as a union indexed by all subsets J ⊂ I, possibly infinitely many sets, so 'réunion de fermés donc fermé' does not follow. A correct argument: ∩(A_i∪B_i) = (∩A_i) ∪ (T ∩ ∩_i((A_i∩T)∪B_i)). The first term is τ-closed; the second is an intersection of τ'_0-closed subsets of T.
Slip: he says the union is 'un fermé de (S,τ)'. The terms with J ≠ I are only of the form A∪B (τ'-closed), not τ-closed.

The converse (any τ' ≤ τ with the prescribed traces on T and U equals this τ') is false in general. Such τ' can be strictly finer via condition 3. He rightly crossed it out and replaced it by the closure condition on p.40.

ideas.what: Coarsest topology finer than τ inducing a prescribed finer topology on a closed subset; closed sets = A∪B
ideas.modern_name: join of topologies / extension of a topology from a closed subspace

ideas.what: Characterisation of closed sets via traces on U and T plus the condition cl(X_U)∩T ⊂ X_T
ideas.modern_name: recollement / Artin gluing of an open U and closed complement T (gluing condition)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé IV (recollement de topos) - sheaf-theoretic analogue

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary general topology, worked out by hand as a lemma for his 'algebra of figures'. It is correct in substance, with a small gap in the infinite-intersection step. The implicit link to open/closed recollement is standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 6: '[?] affine τ' should likely read 'plus fine que τ' ("qui soit plus fine que τ").
'On a [?] unique partie [?] des conditions' probably reads 'On a une [topologie] unique partie satisfaisant les conditions' or similar; illegible.
Margin: 'Soit x condition que' is probably 'Soit X ; condition pour que X soit fermé', with X a subset, not a point x. Also 'B ⊃ x∩T' should be B = X∩T and 'U = X∩(S∖T)'.
